description: torch.geqrf spends 79% in the relaunched, memory-bound geqr2 panel kernel. Write a custom Triton blocked-Householder QR, one CTA per matrix: factor a width-b column panel kept resident in shared memory (sequential reflector loop), form the T factor, then apply the block reflector to the trailing submatrix via tl.dot. Fuse panel+trailing-update to eliminate the thousands of tiny per-step relaunches. Target the batched n=512 cluster (4 of 12 shapes). Emit packed (H,tau); FP32 reflectors; pass all ill-conditioned guards. Tune b in {16,32,64}.

Small-n shapes (n in {32,176,352}) are dominated by torch.geqrf launch overhead and per-panel relaunches, yet count equally in the geomean. Write a custom Triton fully-resident QR for n<=352: one CTA (or warp-group) per matrix factors the ENTIRE matrix in shared memory/registers with zero trailing relaunches (unblocked or single-block Householder, sequential reflector loop), writing packed (H,tau) once. FP32; pass rankdef/clustered/nearcollinear guards. Maximize batch occupancy across the 20-40 matrices per shape.

Exploit the n-scaled factor tolerance (rtol=20*n*eps32) to run GEMM-heavy trailing updates on tensor cores at reduced precision in Triton. Blocked Householder QR where panel factorization, reflectors and tau stay FP32, but the larfb-style trailing update V*(T^T*(V^T*A)) runs via tl.dot in TF32/FP16 with FP32 accumulate; re-orthogonalize if needed to hold the 100*n*eps32 orthogonality gate. Verify rankdef/nearrank/nearcollinear/clustered still pass. Emit packed (H,tau).

The global best (4.32x) fuses a Triton col-tile blocked-Householder kernel but only for n=512; n=1024 still falls back to torch.geqrf and now dominates the geomean (3 of 12 shapes, batch=60, ~221ms each, the largest log terms). Extend the fused panel-factor + col-tile trailing-update Triton kernel to n=1024: re-tile for the 1024-wide matrix with tuned panel width B and RT/CT, or go multi-CTA-per-matrix. Keep per-CTA shared memory <=101KB (sm_120 optin limit; prefer multi-CTA over wider tiles), packed (H,tau), FP32, pass all guards. Add n=1024 to the verified grid.

Combine the small-n Triton wins with the fused n=512/1024 kernel into one multi-size dispatch. Parent A (48a40e42, your brief-0) has the fully-resident Triton QR for n=32 (12.7x) and n=176 (1.57x); parent B (76ac9b27, global best) has the fused col-tile blocked-Householder for n=512/1024. Merge both kernels into one submission.py, routing each n to its verified path via a clean size->path table (n in {32,176}->resident; {512,1024}->fused; all else incl off-grid->geqrf) with explicit fallback. The n=32 shape's outsized log-space weight makes this a large geomean win. Keep packed (H,tau) FP32; all 22 tests + 3 guards CLEAN per path; watch for kernel-name/autotune-cache collisions between the two merged kernels.

Extend the fused Triton blocked-Householder kernel (global best, currently n=512/1024) to the remaining geqrf-fallback shapes, biggest proven win first. PRIMARY n=352 (batch40): torch.geqrf hits its m>256 cuSOLVER domino cliff here (your own 3.82x discovery measured n=352->2x via cliff-dodge), so the fused Triton path should beat it -- add n=352 to the grid (next_pow2=512 tiles; tune B/RT/CT/VT for the batch-40 occupancy). SECONDARY n=2048 (batch8): Worker 1 verified the fused kernel does ~1.2x as-is at B=32 VT=128 -- add it. Keep n=4096 (batch2) on torch.geqrf (verified 25x slower, only 2 CTAs). Do not regress any shape. Packed (H,tau) FP32; all 22 tests + 3 guards CLEAN.

Break the panel-factor 16%-occupancy ceiling (1 block/SM, capped by the 64KB resident [n,B] smem tile + 220 regs/thread) -- it bottlenecks BOTH n=512 and n=1024 (7 of 12 shapes), so a win compounds. Replace the one-CTA-per-matrix sequential panel with a TSQR / communication-avoiding factorization: split each matrix's tall panel into row-blocks factored by SEPARATE CTAs (far more CTAs -> fills all 188 SMs, each block's smem is small/non-resident), then merge the R-blocks (binary-tree or single combiner). CRITICAL RISK to retire first: emitting a single geqrf-compatible packed (H,tau) from tree-merged reflectors is fragile -- mitigate by computing R via TSQR then doing ONE re-factor pass of the panel against the final R to produce canonical reflectors, rather than merging tree reflectors directly. Keep the existing multi-CTA col-tile trailing update and CHUNK L2-blocking. Packed (H,tau) FP32, geqrf-grade accuracy; all 22 tests + 3 guards CLEAN; don't regress any shape.

Combine the two sibling branches with disjoint wins into one full-coverage dispatch. Parent A (540eeca3, current global best 13.21x) has the fused kernel for n in {352,512,1024,2048} but reverted n=32/176 to slow geqrf. Parent B (62e3459f, your own combine, 12.49x) has the fast resident Triton kernel for n in {32,176}. Take A as the base (most fused coverage) and graft B's _resident_qr_kernel + dispatch so n in {32,176}->resident, {352,512,1024,2048}->fused, else (incl n=4096 and off-grid)->geqrf. Recovering n=32 (288us->22.6us, outsized log weight) on top of 13.21x should reach ~17x. Both kernel bodies are byte-identical to their verified parents; distinct @triton.jit names, no autotune (no cache collision). Packed (H,tau) FP32; all 22 tests + 3 guards CLEAN; verify each path is exercised.

Fold Worker 0's L2 cache-blocking into the full-coverage global best. Parent A (6266257b, current best 17.02x) has all 11 custom-shape paths but NO CHUNK cache-blocking. Parent B (52cd7e1c, Worker 0) added CHUNK=160 batch-chunking to the n=512 path so each chunk's working set stays L2-resident, cutting the HBM-bound trailing kernel reads (n=512 12.2ms->10.9ms, ~11%). Graft B's CHUNK loop + per-n CHUNK config onto A's _qr_custom host loop, keeping n=1024/2048 unchunked (W0 proved their grids are already underfilled so chunking starves them - CHUNK huge for those). Touch only the host-side chunk loop; kernels byte-identical. ~4 of 12 shapes improve ~11% => ~+4% geomean. Packed (H,tau) FP32; all 22 tests + 3 guards CLEAN; re-confirm no shape regresses.

Attack the two largest remaining log-space terms, both small-batch large-n still slow: n=4096 (batch2, ~48ms, on geqrf) and n=2048 (batch8, ~61ms, fused only 1.20x). Both starve the one-CTA-per-matrix panel factor (2-8 CTAs on 188 SMs). geqrf at n=4096 runs only ~5 TFLOPS (far below ~125 peak) => NOT compute-bound, real headroom. Pursue MULTI-CTA-PER-MATRIX panel factorization: split each matrix's tall panel across CTAs (row-block norm reductions, two-pass) to manufacture enough CTAs to fill the GPU from tiny batch -- this is the OPPOSITE regime from the n=512/1024 smem-reduction ceiling (Worker 0 proved TSQR can't help THAT, but here the problem is too-few-CTAs, not too-many). Use TF32 tensor-core trailing (you proved it's safe at n>=2048 under the n-scaled tolerance). Keep multi-CTA col-tile trailing. Add n=4096 to the grid only if it beats geqrf; don't regress. Packed (H,tau) FP32 output; all 22 tests + 3 guards CLEAN.

You proved TSQR can't break the panel occupancy ceiling (irreducible under packed-(H,tau)) -- so pivot to the ORTHOGONAL lever you measured: tf32 tensor-core trailing is ~5% faster at n=512 but fails the factor gate (scaled residual 27.5>20) on clustered/ill-conditioned inputs UNCORRECTED. Make it SAFE for n=512/1024: run the larfb-style trailing update V*(T^T*(V^T*A)) in tf32 (or bf16) tensor cores with FP32 accumulate, then recover accuracy via a correction -- e.g. one step of iterative refinement on the trailing residual, or compute the trailing update in tf32 then add an fp32 low-rank correction for the dropped mantissa bits. Panel factorization + reflectors + tau stay exact FP32. Target: capture the ~5% trailing speedup on n=512/1024 (7 of 12 shapes) while passing the clustered/rankdef/band factor gate (20*n*eps) and the 100*n*eps orthogonality gate. If correction costs more than the tf32 saving, that's a valid negative finding. Packed (H,tau) FP32; all 22 tests + 3 guards CLEAN; don't regress.

n=176 (batch40) is the WEAKEST custom shape: only 1.6x (9873us) on the resident kernel, a large log-space term. Packed (H,tau) FP32; all 22 tests + 3 guards CLEAN; don't regress any shape.

Your single-kernel n=512/1024 levers are tapped (occupancy ceiling irreducible, trailing bandwidth-bound, precision dead) -- so attack UTILIZATION across kernels: both the panel-factor (~16% occ, compute/latency-bound) and the trailing (~16% occ, bandwidth-bound) leave ~84% of SMs idle, and different batch-CHUNKs are fully independent. Pipeline them with CUDA streams: process chunk B's panel-factor concurrently with chunk A's trailing (offset by one phase) so the occupancy-bound panel overlaps the bandwidth-bound trailing and fills idle SMs. Target n=512 (batch640, 4 chunks) primarily, n=1024 if it helps. CRITICAL tension to measure: 2 concurrent chunks ~double the L2 working set and may break the CHUNK=160 L2-residency win -- sweep chunk size / stream count to find the overlap-vs-L2 sweet spot. If stream overlap can't beat the serial CHUNK baseline, that's a valid negative finding. Packed (H,tau) FP32; all 22 tests + 3 guards CLEAN; don't regress n=1024/2048/352/4096.
